$comment: Archive manifest. URLs written from knowledge of these collections; verified:false means the locator has not been resolved in this session. Resolve before citing. Nothing large is committed to this repo - use scripts/fetch-archives.mjs for public-domain texts.

archives.title: Southern Horrors: Lynch Law in All Its Phases
archives.author: Ida B. Wells
archives.note: Wells's method: refute the stated pretext for each lynching using the white press's own reporting of it.

archives.title: A Red Record: Tabulated Statistics and Alleged Causes of Lynching in the United States, 1892-1893-1894
archives.author: Ida B. Wells
archives.note: The direct ancestor of this record book: a tabulated log of killings with alleged cause set against investigated cause.

archives.title: Mob Rule in New Orleans
archives.author: Ida B. Wells

archives.title: Crusade for Justice: The Autobiography of Ida B. Wells
archives.author: Ida B. Wells; Alfreda M. Duster, ed.
archives.note: Source for the People's Grocery killings and for Thomas Moss's recorded last words.

archives.title: Thirty Years of Lynching in the United States, 1889-1918
archives.author: National Association for the Advancement of Colored People
archives.note: Enumerates 3,224 persons lynched over the period. The canonical aggregate complaint log of the era.

archives.title: Papers of the NAACP
archives.note: Branch files, anti-lynching campaign files, and legal department case files. Walter White's field investigations are here. Also distributed as ProQuest History Vault.

archives.title: Born in Slavery: Slave Narratives from the Federal Writers' Project, 1936-1938
archives.note: Approximately 2,300 first-person accounts and 500 photographs. Read with care for the interview conditions: most interviewers were white, most narrators were dependent on New Deal relief, and the transcription conventions were imposed.

archives.title: North American Slave Narratives (Documenting the American South)
archives.holder: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Libraries
archives.note: Full-text narratives published to 1920, including Douglass, Jacobs, Equiano, Bibb, Northup.

archives.title: Records of the Bureau of Refugees, Freedmen, and Abandoned Lands (Record Group 105)
archives.holder: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration
archives.note: Materially important to this book: the Bureau's registers of complaints and reports of outrages are the closest surviving analogue to a contemporaneous complaint log, and record both the injury and the refusal of local courts to hear it.

archives.title: Chronicling America: Historic American Newspapers
archives.holder: Library of Congress / National Endowment for the Humanities
archives.note: Searchable full text. Includes Black press titles. Supports the Wells method directly: the white press's own contemporaneous account is often the strongest evidence against the coroner's finding.

archives.title: Lynching in America: Confronting the Legacy of Racial Terror
archives.author: Equal Justice Initiative
archives.note: Documents over 4,400 racial terror lynchings, 1877-1950, with county-level data.

archives.title: Civil Rights and Restorative Justice Project: Burnham-Nobles Digital Archive
archives.note: The closest existing institution to what this book is: documented anti-Black homicides, 1930-1970, with the disposition of each case. Where an entry here is thin, check CRRJ first.

archives.title: Reports to Congress under the Emmett Till Unsolved Civil Rights Crime Act
archives.holder: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division
archives.note: The official record of which cold cases were reopened and why each was closed. Nearly all closures cite the death of all identified subjects.

archives.title: Final Report of the Oklahoma Commission to Study the Tulsa Race Riot of 1921
A Documented History of the Incident Which Occurred at Rosewood, Florida, in January 1923
archives.holder: Florida Board of Regents / Florida State Archives
archives.note: The study commissioned by the Florida Legislature that produced the 1994 compensation act.

archives.title: 1898 Wilmington Race Riot Commission Report
archives.holder: North Carolina Office of Archives and History

archives.title: National Registry of Exonerations
archives.holder: University of Michigan Law School, Michigan State University, University of California Irvine
archives.note: Contemporary continuation of the pattern: documents wrongful convictions and, in the official-misconduct field, conduct by officials that was itself rarely prosecuted.

archives.title: SlaveVoyages: Trans-Atlantic and Intra-American Slave Trade Databases
archives.note: Includes the African Origins name database, which restores given names to individuals recorded in registers of liberated Africans. Directly relevant to the identity problem in METHODOLOGY.md section 9.

archives.title: Digital Library on American Slavery
archives.holder: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
archives.note: Race and Slavery Petitions Project: legislative and county-court petitions, 1775-1867. A genuine antebellum complaint corpus, and evidence of what could and could not be complained of.

archives.title: Tuskegee Institute Lynching Records
archives.note: The annual tally maintained from 1882. Compare against the NAACP and EJI counts; the three series differ in definition and coverage, and the differences are themselves evidence.

archives.title: NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund case records and publications
archives.holder: NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund, Inc.
archives.note: Separate organization from the NAACP since 1957. Source for Groveland, Moore v. Dempsey lineage, and capital defense records.

archives.title: United Negro College Fund
archives.note: Listed for completeness because it was named in the brief. UNCF is a scholarship and member-institution funder, not a crime archive. The archival material is held by its member institutions - Fisk, Howard (not UNCF), Atlanta University Center's Woodruff Library, Tuskegee - whose special collections hold the relevant papers.

archives.title: Moore v. Dempsey, 261 U.S. 86 (1923)
The Shocking Story of Approved Killing in Mississippi
archives.author: William Bradford Huie
archives.note: Paid confession by Bryant and Milam after their acquittal. Double jeopardy barred retrial. The single clearest document of impunity in this book.

archives.title: United States Reports
archives.holder: Supreme Court of the United States
archives.note: The Court's own record of its holdings. Cited here for Dred Scott v. Sandford, 60 U.S. 393 (1857) and United States v. Cruikshank, 92 U.S. 542 (1876). A judicial vantage on entries where the holding is itself the act complained of.

archives.title: Records of the United States Public Health Service Study of Untreated Syphilis in the Negro Male
archives.holder: U.S. National Archives, Southeast Region; Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
archives.note: The perpetrating agency's own forty-year record: enrolment, examination and autopsy files kept meticulously because the men were regarded as subjects rather than as parties who might one day read them. The strongest vantage on that entry belongs to those who ran the study.

archives.title: Mississippi State Sovereignty Commission Records
archives.holder: Mississippi Department of Archives and History
archives.note: Opened by federal court order in 1998 over the state's objection. A perpetrator record in which a state agency documented its own arrangement of prosecutions, including Clyde Kennard's. The rare case where the impediment kept the evidence against itself.

archives.title: National Archives Catalog (API v2)
archives.holder: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration
archives.note: Public JSON API over NARA's descriptive catalogue and digitised holdings. The programmatic entry point to every record group below; scripts/fetch-archives.mjs can query it directly once there is network egress. Requires an API key for sustained use.

archives.title: General Records of the Department of Justice (Record Group 60)
archives.holder: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration
archives.note: Departmental correspondence and case files, including the civil rights era files and the decisions not to prosecute that this book records as no_process and investigated_no_charge. The file that explains a non-prosecution is usually here rather than in any court record.

archives.title: Records of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (Record Group 65)
archives.holder: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration
archives.note: Investigative case files. Relevant to Moore's Ford (the 1946 investigation, some 2,790 interviews, no indictment), Groveland, and the Till Act cold case reviews.

archives.title: Records of the District Courts of the United States (Record Group 21)
archives.holder: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration
archives.note: Case files, dockets and grand jury records of the federal trial courts, including the Enforcement Act prosecutions that produced the Colfax convictions later vacated in Cruikshank.

archives.title: Report of the Joint Select Committee to Inquire into the Condition of Affairs in the Late Insurrectionary States (1872)
archives.holder: U.S. Congress; digitised by the Library of Congress and HathiTrust
archives.note: Thirteen volumes of sworn testimony taken from freedpeople and others across the South in 1871. One of the largest bodies of first-person testimony about Reconstruction-era violence ever collected, given under oath, by people who were still living where the violence occurred. Very little of it produced a prosecution.

archives.title: National Museum of African American History and Culture
archives.note: Collection, digital resources, and the Slave Wrecks Project. Holds objects whose provenance is itself the record - shackles, a slave cabin, Emmett Till's casket.

archives.title: The Legacy Museum and the National Memorial for Peace and Justice
archives.note: The memorial names over 4,400 lynching victims on 800 county monuments, one per county. It is the closest existing physical analogue to this register: an attempt to convert a tally back into named individuals, county by county, which is the standing task recorded in this repository's README.

archives.title: Whitney Plantation Museum
archives.note: The only US plantation museum told from the perspective of the enslaved. Its memorials inscribe names drawn from the Louisiana Slave Database and quotations from the WPA narratives, which makes it a rare instance of a narrative-preserving institution doing the individuation work this book's register calls for.

archives.title: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
archives.note: Manuscripts, oral histories, photographs and the Digital Schomburg. A primary holder for twentieth-century Black organisational and personal papers.

archives.title: Moorland-Spingarn Research Center
archives.note: One of the largest repositories of materials on the global Black experience. Holds the papers of many figures whose organisations appear in this book.

archives.title: Amistad Research Center
archives.note: American Missionary Association archives and extensive civil rights organisational records.

archives.title: Avery Research Center for African American History and Culture
archives.note: Lowcountry and Gullah Geechee collections, oral histories, and family papers.

archives.title: Center for Family History, International African American Museum
archives.note: Built on the site of Gadsden's Wharf. Its genealogical centre exists to restore descent lines severed by sale - the harm this book records as interstitial under chattel enslavement, addressed directly.

archives.title: Behind the Veil: Documenting African American Life in the Jim Crow South
archives.holder: Duke University, Rubenstein Library / Center for Documentary Studies
archives.note: Approximately 1,300 recorded interviews with people who lived under segregation, collected in the 1990s. The single most important corpus for this book after the WPA narratives: first-person testimony about the period most of these entries fall in, given by people who survived it and were never asked at the time.

archives.title: National Civil Rights Museum at the Lorraine Motel
archives.note: Memphis is the site of the People's Grocery killings and the destruction of the Free Speech, both entered in this log.

archives.title: Emmett Till Interpretive Center and the Emmett Till Memory Project
archives.holder: Emmett Till Interpretive Center, Sumner, Mississippi
archives.note: Sited at the courthouse where the acquittal was returned. Documents the markers themselves, which have been repeatedly shot and replaced - a continuing act against the record that the record now keeps.

archives.title: Post Traumatic Slave Syndrome: America's Legacy of Enduring Injury and Healing
archives.author: Joy DeGruy (published as Joy DeGruy Leary)
archives.holder: Uptone Press; revised edition, Joy DeGruy Publications, 2017
archives.note: The framework for generational harm this record book had no field for until it was added. DeGruy argues that multigenerational trauma from chattel slavery and continuing oppression, without opportunity to heal, produces adaptive survival behaviours - she names vacant esteem, ever-present anger, and racist socialisation. IMPORTANT: PTSS is an influential theoretical and clinical framework, widely taught and used in practice; it is not a diagnostic category in the DSM and parts of the intergenerational-transmission literature it draws on remain contested. This book records it as a contested vantage, which is what it is, and not as an established finding.

archives.title: Post Traumatic Slave Syndrome: Study Guide and companion workbook
archives.author: Joy DeGruy
archives.note: The applied companion to the monograph, used in community and clinical settings.

archives.title: Joy DeGruy: scholarly articles, instruments, and lectures
archives.author: Joy DeGruy
archives.holder: Portland State University School of Social Work; joydegruy.com
archives.note: Her work beyond the book: doctoral and faculty research in social work at Portland State, the African American Respect Scale developed to measure respect within Black families, and a large recorded lecture corpus. UNRESOLVED: the specific bibliography of the monograph, and a complete list of her published articles, could not be retrieved - this session has no network egress. Pull them from the book's notes and from a library database before citing any of it. Nothing in this manifest should be read as a reconstruction of her citations.

archives.title: Historical trauma and intergenerational transmission: the scholarly field
archives.note: The body of work DeGruy's framework sits within and argues alongside. Principal figures: Maria Yellow Horse Brave Heart on historical trauma and historical unresolved grief among the Lakota, which introduced the term to the clinical literature; Eduardo and Bonnie Duran on the soul wound in Native American Postcolonial Psychology (1995); Yael Danieli, ed., International Handbook of Multigenerational Legacies of Trauma (1998); Rachel Yehuda on biological correlates of transmission in offspring of Holocaust survivors; Na'im Akbar, Chains and Images of Psychological Slavery (1984); Kenneth and Mamie Clark's doll studies, cited in Brown v. Board of Education; W.E.B. Du Bois on double consciousness; Frantz Fanon. THIS IS A LINEAGE, NOT A BIBLIOGRAPHY. It records the field, assembled from knowledge of it and not retrieved in this session. It is not a reconstruction of what DeGruy cites, and must not be presented as one. Verify every author, title and date against the works themselves before use.
